items.description: B-roll POV dinâmico de um conjunto de copos, destacando transparência, formato, reflexos, detalhes e manuseio realista.
items.prompt:
GOOGLE FLOW — VIDEO ELEMENTS

DYNAMIC POV GLASSWARE SET B-ROLL

DURATION: 8 seconds
FORMAT: Vertical 9:16
STYLE: Ultra-realistic smartphone UGC product video.
CAMERA: Authentic first-person POV.
EDITING: 6 dynamic action-driven microtakes.

HERO ELEMENT:
The exact glassware set shown in the attached original Product Element.

ACTIVITY FOCUS:
Present the original glassware set dynamically, highlighting the authentic glass transparency, shape, thickness, rim, base, surface texture, decorative details and real light reflections through natural first-person handling and energetic product B-roll.

REFERENCE LOCK — CRITICAL:

Preserve EXACTLY the original glassware design from the reference.

Maintain:
- Exact glass shape and silhouette.
- Original number of glasses in the set.
- Original relative sizes and proportions.
- Actual glass color and transparency.
- Original rim thickness and shape.
- Real stems and bases, if present.
- Existing decorative patterns, facets or textures.
- Original surface finish.
- Realistic glass material and optical behavior.

Do not invent decorative patterns, engraving, stems, handles or details absent from the reference.

Every glass must remain visually identical to its original referenced design throughout the video.

SCENE:

Real contemporary Brazilian home.

Natural kitchen or dining room environment.

The original glassware set is arranged on a clean, realistic dining table.

Soft daylight enters from a nearby window, creating authentic reflections and gentle light transmission through the glass.

Subtle everyday background details, without visual clutter.

The product remains the central focus.

True first-person camera perspective looking at the glassware from a natural standing or slightly leaning position.

Only realistic hands and forearms appear when interacting with the product.

DYNAMIC B-ROLL SEQUENCE:

SHOT 1 — 0.0–1.0s
DYNAMIC PRODUCT REVEAL

Start with the original glassware set already arranged on the table.

Quick natural handheld camera movement from a slightly elevated angle toward the glasses.

The camera makes a small lateral approach, creating natural parallax between the individual glasses.

Daylight reflects and refracts through the real glass surfaces.

Clearly establish the original set and its quantity.

SHOT 2 — 1.0–2.3s
NATURAL PICKUP

Action-matched cut toward one glass from the original set.

A realistic hand approaches and gently grips the glass at an anatomically appropriate location for its actual design.

Fingers make natural contact with the surface.

A small grip correction happens before the glass is lifted.

The hand raises the glass a short distance above the table.

Realistic weight, inertia and hand stabilization.

Natural reflections shift across the glass as it moves.

SHOT 3 — 2.3–3.6s
MACRO-STYLE GLASS DETAIL

Dynamic close-up of the same glass being held.

The camera physically approaches the existing rim and upper surface.

Show authentic rim thickness, transparent material, real optical refraction and existing decorative details, if any.

The hand rotates the glass slightly and naturally to reveal another visible angle.

Light travels through the material realistically, with subtle highlights and accurate background distortion.

Small smartphone autofocus correction.

No artificial glowing glass or fake digital macro zoom.

SHOT 4 — 3.6–5.0s
SIDE DETAIL AND GLASS STRUCTURE

Fast action-matched cut to a closer side angle.

The same glass remains in the hand.

A gentle wrist rotation reveals the original body shape and lower structure.

Show existing facets, texture, stem or base only if those features exist in the actual reference.

The camera makes a short lateral movement, creating a realistic change in reflections and transparency.

The hand slightly adjusts its grip with natural timing.

No sudden glass design changes.

SHOT 5 — 5.0–6.5s
SATISFYING PLACEMENT AND DETAIL

The hand naturally lowers the glass onto the table.

The real base contacts the tabletop with a delicate, authentic glass contact sound.

The fingers gradually release pressure.

The glass makes a tiny natural settling movement and remains upright.

Quick close-up of the real base, rim or existing decorative feature, emphasizing the fine material and craftsmanship.

A small camera reframing correction follows the movement.

SHOT 6 — 6.5–8.0s
FINAL FULL SET PAYOFF

Dynamic cut to a slightly wider first-person angle showing the complete original glassware set arranged together.

The glass previously handled is present in its new position.

A hand makes a small final adjustment to align one glass naturally.

Camera makes a subtle handheld lateral reveal, allowing natural highlights and reflections to shift across the set.

End with a clear, attractive composition displaying all the original glasses.

Every glass remains the exact same referenced design.

VISUAL DETAIL PRIORITY:

Emphasize the physical qualities actually present in the product:

Real transparent or colored glass.
Authentic material thickness.
Accurate edge highlights.
Natural light refraction.
Realistic environmental reflections.
Subtle imperfections in reflections.
Original glass shape.
Existing decorative patterns and textures.
Realistic contact with the tabletop.

The glass must look physically real, not like CGI or acrylic.

CAMERA ENGINE:

Recent smartphone main camera.
1x lens, approximately 24–26mm equivalent.
Vertical 9:16.

Authentic POV handheld filming.

Short energetic camera movements.
Natural perspective changes.
Brief physical push-ins.
Action-matched hard cuts.
Small lateral movements.
Real autofocus adjustments.
Subtle exposure adaptation.
Natural smartphone sharpening.
Realistic physical motion blur.
Very subtle sensor noise.

For macro-style detail shots, move the camera physically closer while maintaining realistic smartphone focusing distance.

Do not simulate an impossible microscopic lens.

Avoid excessive digital zoom.
Avoid artificial cinematic orbit.
Avoid perfect gimbal stabilization.
Avoid fake HDR and studio glow.

NATURAL HUMAN MOTION:

Hands must move spontaneously.

Small hesitation before contact.
Natural acceleration while lifting.
Subtle grip pressure.
Minor finger repositioning.
Real wrist rotation.
Small overshoot.
Realistic deceleration.
Natural release of the glass.
Brief settling after contact.

No perfectly repeated gestures.
No robotic hand movements.
No exaggerated commercial acting.

HAND REALISM:

Exactly five fingers per visible hand.

Natural skin pores and texture.
Correct knuckles and joints.
Real fingernails and cuticles.
Natural asymmetry.
Real finger pressure.
Physically correct grip.
Accurate contact shadows.

No extra fingers.
No merged fingers.
No hands passing through glass.

GLASS PHYSICS ENGINE:

The glasses have real mass, weight and rigidity.

Glass cannot bend, stretch or change shape.

Transparent surfaces must preserve realistic refraction and reflections.

Hands must physically support the glass before lifting.

Every glass stays in the correct physical location unless moved by visible contact.

The glass base rests naturally on the table.

No floating.
No teleportation.
No material transformation.
No impossible collisions.
No duplicated glassware.

OBJECT PERMANENCE:

The original Product Element remains the absolute source of truth.

The glass being lifted is the SAME glass being rotated, examined and placed back onto the table.

The quantity of glasses remains consistent.

Do not introduce extra glasses during close-ups.

Do not replace the original design with a generic wine glass or another glassware model.

Do not invent stems, bases, handles, patterns or engravings.

Every cut preserves the original product identity.

DYNAMIC EDITING RULES:

Every shot must reveal new visual information.

Shot 1: Complete set.
Shot 2: Physical interaction.
Shot 3: Rim and material close-up.
Shot 4: Shape and structural detail.
Shot 5: Real placement and finishing detail.
Shot 6: Complete set final reveal.

Fast, satisfying rhythm.

Cuts follow physical actions.

Never repeat an identical beauty shot.

Keep natural product handling more important than camera effects.

ANTI-BUG:

No glass changing design.
No changing glass quantity.
No invented decorative details.
No additional products.
No floating glassware.
No glass morphing.
No fake transparent plastic.
No unrealistic rainbow reflections.
No artificial glowing edges.
No impossible camera movements.
No hands clipping through glass.
No duplicated fingers.
No robotic motion.
No slow motion.
No artificial studio perfection.

FAIL-SAFE:

If product geometry becomes unstable during rotation, reduce the rotation angle and use a smaller natural wrist movement.

If extreme close-ups threaten the original design, maintain a realistic close-up distance and emphasize actual visible details.

If reflections become artificial, simplify the lighting to natural window daylight.

Preserve product fidelity while maintaining dynamic camera movement and realistic human interaction.

AUDIO:

Authentic quiet indoor ambience.

Soft hand contact with glass.

Very subtle glass handling sounds.

Delicate glass-to-table contact.

Natural room tone.

No music.
No voiceover.
No exaggerated glass clinking.

Dialogue: sem fala.
items.tips: Preservar exatamente o conjunto original, inclusive quantidade, geometria, transparência, espessura e detalhes existentes.
